properties.helpText:
*LLCs are like “tax chameleons” and can elect to be treated as disregarded entities (sole proprietorships), partnerships, or corporations (either S-corporations or C-corporations)*

*Single-member LLCs often elect “sole proprietorship”, in which case the LLC will be “disregarded” for tax purposes. A husband and wife are treated as one person for tax purposes, so the LLC will be “disregarded” for Federal tax purposes if a married couple elects “sole proprietorship.”*

*If there are two or more members who are unmarried, the LLC will be taxed as a “partnership”, unless an election is made on a Federal Tax Form filed with the Internal Revenue Service to be taxed as a corporation. An LLC taxes as a partnership will be required to file a partnership tax return.* 

*An LLC may elect to be taxed as a corporation (whether an S-corporation or a C-corporation), whether a single or multi-member LLC. Consult with your tax advisor if you are unsure about the proper election and absolutely before electing to be taxed as a corporation, whether an S-corporation or a C-corporation.*
properties.name: IncomeTaxElection

properties.name: NAICSCode
properties.label: Select the appropriate NAICS Code for this entity.
properties.helpText:
A NAICS (pronounced NAKES) code is a six-digit number used by federal statistical agencies in the United States, Canada, and Mexico to classify businesses according to their primary economic activity.

The primary purpose of NAICS is to collect, analyze, and publish statistical data related to the U.S. business economy, providing a standardized way to categorize industries. It replaced the older Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system in 1997.
